quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane to see other vehicles better.
Ride close behind the vehicle in front of you to use their headlights.
Slow down to help you avoid hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to help you avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your distance from other vehicles and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and change it as needed.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: You must stay aware of your surroundings. Do not depend only on mirrors. Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. If you turn too fast, you may leave your lane or go off the road.

questions.question: Which brake is stronger on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to operate a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to safely ride. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane or block your way out if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ maintenance.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent maintenance than cars. Find and fix problems before riding in traffic or at high speeds.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Should you wear hearing protection?

options.text: No, not needed if you wear a helmet.

questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Always wear hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase the distance between you and other vehicles to avoid crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: More time to react to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to move safely.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if it takes longer to stop, you cannot see ahead clearly, or traffic is heavy with vehicles trying to squeeze in front of you.

questions.question: Which lane position best prevents other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane

questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing into your lane. When behind a car, the center position makes you visible in the middle of their rearview mirror, where drivers are most likely to see you.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing at all times when riding.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding is to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Scan the road well ahead to spot dangers early. Watch for hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to grip your hips, waist, or belt firmly. They may also use secure handholds if available.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection without traffic lights at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
